Our case study is: 


### Case Study: FiveThirtyEight:
## [Uber Is Taking Millions Of Manhattan Rides Away From Taxis](https://fivethirtyeight.com/features/uber-is-taking-millions-of-manhattan-rides-away-from-taxis/)

*There was not a case study with data visualizations about park effects in baseball, so we looked at a story about NYC taxis. We used the visualizations from this case study as inspiration for our report.*

- This report includes many types of visualizations and types of graphs including:
 - Line graphs with multiple observations
 - Maps (spatial maps with facet wraps)
 - Tables
 - Plots with best fits and labeled points
 - Finally, the report reads like a story with text in between graphs, describing the relationship of taxi rides and time with the introduction of Uber.
 
 
  **How does the report build the data story in the Case Study Page**
 
 + We took inspiration from the multiple variables visualized in the case study, so we made graphs with multiple variables in our report by changing:
 - Color of points
 - Fill
 - size
 - Logos
 - Including different visualizations not included in the case study:
  - Boxplots
  - Density
